title: Reduced boundary of a smooth curve is smooth of dimension zero
statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field (every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable), let $C$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $j:U\to C$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $i:Z\to C$ be the reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] closed complement [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $Z$ is a finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] $k$-scheme with $\dim Z\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (and $\dim Z=-\infty$ when $Z=\varnothing$), and its structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of pure relative dimension zero [def-weil-pure-dimension].

source.place: Step 2: the reduced scheme Z is a finite disjoint union of spectra of perfect fields, hence smooth of dimension zero

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $C=\bigcup_{a=1}^m\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ with each $A_a$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], the preimage in $Z$ of the $a$th member is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$ for an ideal $I_a\subseteq A_a$. The images of any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A_a$ generate $A_a/I_a$. These finitely many quotient spectra cover $Z$, proving that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by the same definition. Reducedness of $Z$ is part of the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), closed-immersion assertion, written out on the given finite affine cover

proof.text: Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C$ is contained in an irreducible component: apply [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] to its largest member. The chain remains a chain of closed irreducible subsets of that component. Each component has dimension one by [def-weil-pure-dimension], so the topological Krull dimension of $C$ is at most one (also when $C$ is empty). By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], this is the dimension hypothesis of [lem-pc-nowhere-dense-dim-zero]. The subset $|Z|=|C|\setminus U$ is closed with empty interior because $U$ is dense. Thus that lemma applies to the closed immersion $i$ and yields $\dim Z\le0$. Apply [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $Z$ to express this as topological Krull dimension at most zero. If $Z$ is empty both dimensions in this comparison are $-\infty$, as explicitly included in the comparison lemma.

source.place: Tag 0AYY (lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor), proof sentence deducing dimension at most zero from nowhere density; dimension comparison: Properties Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ of step 1 and the topological dimension bound of step 2. Its statement gives that $|Z|$ is finite and discrete; in particular every singleton $\{z\}$ is both open and closed. For every $z\in Z$, write $Z_z$ for the open subscheme on $\{z\}$. This construction has no members when $Z$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0AAX (lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0), discrete underlying space; Varieties Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), finite type gives finitely many summands

proof.text: Each singleton scheme $Z_z$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]; put $B_z=\Gamma(Z_z,\mathcal O_Z)$. The only open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z_z$ is $Z_z$, so the stalk is $B_z$ itself. Thus $B_z$ is a nonzero local ring and is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Since $\operatorname{Spec}B_z$ has just one point, $B_z$ has exactly one prime ideal $\mathfrak m_z$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. This prime is minimal. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], $(B_z)_{\mathfrak m_z}$ is a field. The map $B_z\to(B_z)_{\mathfrak m_z}$ is an isomorphism: every denominator lies outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $B_z$, hence is a unit, and the inverse sends $b/s$ to $bs^{-1}$. Consequently $B_z$ is a field, its maximal ideal is zero, and its quotient defining the residue field in [def-weil-residue-field] identifies $B_z$ with $\kappa_Z(z)$. These maps respect the $k$-algebra structures induced by $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, giving $Z_z\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Z(z)$ over $k$.

source.place: Tag 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring), applied to each singleton affine ring; singleton decomposition: Varieties Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof.text: Every $z\in Z$ is a closed point of the finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$, so part (a) of [lem-kun-closed-point-field] makes $\kappa_Z(z)/k$ finite. It is separable because $k$ is perfect, using the meaning of perfect specified in the statement. Form the coproduct of the finitely many $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Z(z)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The isomorphisms of step 4 identify its summands with the disjoint open subschemes $Z_z$. Their inclusions define a map from the coproduct to $Z$; the inverse maps $Z_z$ to the corresponding summand. The inverses glue since the opens are disjoint and cover $Z$, and the two composites are the identity on every member of these open covers. Hence $Z\simeq\coprod_{z\in |Z|}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_Z(z)$ over $k$. The same gluing argument includes the empty coproduct.

source.place: Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), singleton decomposition and finite residue algebras; Schemes Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), disjoint gluing

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale] to the finite separable extensions $\kappa_Z(z)/k$ obtained in step 5. Under the displayed $k$-isomorphism its coproduct structure morphism is exactly $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so this morphism is etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] it is smooth and its fibres have dimension zero at every source point, that is, it is smooth of pure relative dimension zero. If $Z=\varnothing$, the coproduct theorem applies with empty index set and the relative dimension condition has no points to check. Together with steps 1 and 2 this gives every asserted conclusion, including the empty boundary.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), converse direction; Tag 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified) and the remark after Definition 02GI (definition-etale): etale is smooth of relative dimension zero
